blindSummary:
This state/province is the clearest case in the country of a government reversing course on trans rights within one election cycle. A 2020 policy originally protected LGBTQIA+ student privacy and inclusion. In July 2023 the government amended it to require parental consent for under-16 name/pronoun use, triggering protests outside the legislature. The successor government reversed the amendment in December 2024, effective 1 January 2025: parental consent is now "encouraged but no longer required" for students of any age, with a "presumed capacity" concept based on recommendations from an independent child-rights advocate office. The revised policy text extends its language to "people visiting schools" (student teachers, visiting professionals), so current rules technically reach non-residents presenting in classrooms.

Real risk sits slightly below the country-wide average. The reversal is a strong positive institutional response — a government that legislated against trans students repealed the provision after one term. The residual signal is the demonstrated capacity for hostile policy within an election cycle and the 2023 protest period, which create a slightly higher baseline of political volatility than states/provinces that never legislated against trans people. No street-level disruption of public expression events was documented.

Compared to the two neighbouring states/provinces that invoked a constitutional override power to shield their trans-targeting laws from judicial review, this state/province is materially safer: it never used the override power, and its hostile policy was reversed rather than immunised. The remaining gap to the country-wide picture is small and time-sensitive — the current effective policy is protective, and a further reversal would leave this state/province at or above the country-wide level.
